raw_response:
Well, it's that time of year again. My wheat's been in the ground since last October, and now in April it's coming out of winter and starting to grow again. My maize won't go in until after wheat harvest in June. Let me think through what I'll do this year for both.

My 10.9 mu is all one plot really — I plant the whole thing in wheat in October, then turn right around and plant maize on the same ground in June. That's how everyone does it around here. I've been doing this 20 years, same pattern as my neighbors.

**For the wheat this spring and early summer:**

My wheat is already planted, so what I'm deciding now is how to manage it through to June harvest. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu, which wasn't bad — not as good as Old Wang down the road who always seems to pull 470 or so, but okay for me. Before planting in October I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (that's around 40-50 kg of the 15-15-15 stuff), which my husband says came to maybe 12 kg of nitrogen from the base. Now in the spring when the wheat starts jointing — probably late April — I'll topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu, maybe 20 kg of urea, which is around 9 kg of nitrogen. That's what I did last year and it worked fine.

For water — the winter was a bit dry this year so I already did the winter watering back in December when the ground could take it. I'll probably water again at jointing when I topdress, and then once more at grain filling in May if it doesn't rain. Three waterings total sounds about right. The pump costs me maybe 30-40 yuan per mu each time though, so I don't want to do more than I need to.

I'll spray herbicide once in early spring for the weeds — my neighbor uses the same stuff I do, it's about 15 yuan per mu. If I see aphids later I might spray once, but usually I can get by without.

**For the maize after wheat:**

This is the tight part. Wheat comes off around June 10-12, and I need to get maize in by June 15 at the latest or I lose yield. No time for plowing. I'll hire the neighbor's son who has a direct-seeder — he charges 30 yuan per mu and does it in a day. He puts the seed and some starter fertilizer down together. I'll use the Zhengdan 958 seed, the common one everybody plants, about 2 kg per mu at around 20 yuan.

For fertilizer I'll put down another bag of compound at planting through the seeder, and then topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage in late July, maybe 25 kg of urea per mu. That's what I've settled on over the years. If the maize looks pale I might add a bit more, but usually this is enough.

Maize irrigation — I usually only water once or twice. If June is dry right after planting I'll water to get it up. Then again at tasseling in August if needed. Last year it rained enough and I only watered once.

My husband helps with planting and harvest, and my sister-in-law helps during the busy days. Otherwise I manage the daily work myself. With him doing construction some days, I can't do too much fancy stuff — I need a plan that works even when I'm on my own.

I got about 480 kg of maize per mu last year. I'll hope for similar this year.

Money-wise, I try to keep total input spending under about 700 yuan per mu across both crops. Seeds, fertilizer, water, spraying, and hiring the seeder — it adds up fast, and whatever's left over at the end of the year is what we actually live on.
